newsitem.title: USA: U.S. April budget surplus record $93.94 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. April budget surplus record $93.94 bln.

text.p: The government posted a record budget surplus of $93.94 billion in April, the Treasury Department said on Wednesday, up from a $72.40 billion surplus a year earlier in April 1996.
The April surplus followed a $21.32 billion deficit in March.
April typically produces a surplus because it includes the mid-month filing deadline for individuals to file their prior year's income-tax return.

Revenues from taxes, fees and other sources hit a record $228.59 billion in April, more than double the $108.1 billion taken in during March. A year earlier in April 1996, government revenues were $203.47 billion.
Treasury cited "the impact of large individual tax deposits" as the cause of record April surpluses and revenues.
During the first seven months of fiscal 1997 that ends on Sept 30, the cumulative budget deficit dropped to $16.9 billion from $55.31 billion in the comparable first seven months of fiscal 1996.
Total government outlays in April were $134.65 billion, up from $129.42 billion in March and also up from $131.06 billion a year earlier in April 1996.

Receipts from individual income taxes totaled $134.29 billion in April this year, up from $107.51 billion in April 1996. Corporate income tax receipts rose to $27.42 billion this April from $24.94 billion in April 1996.

The Clinton administration has forecast a budget deficit for the full 1997 fiscal year of $125.59 billion, up from $107.45 billion in fiscal 1996. But primarily because of the strong economy, private analysts expect the deficit to come in much lower than the administration has forecast.
